claims.summary: The training says clients use exposed aliases rather than internal database column names. Explicit numeric types establish value compatibility, not additional public names. UnitCost and AvailableUnits could be client names in an unchanged-name mapping, but this entity exposes cost and available. The frozen catalog continues to supply the already resolved maturity context.

The frozen training declares DECIMAL(10,2) and INT columns before demonstrating unquoted 100 and 0 in typed GraphQL gt filters, and states that input types depend on field types. The repaired stem supplies those numeric SQL types and explicitly states that the published gt inputs accept unquoted integer literals. This supports the offered filter without guessing generated GraphQL type names or deriving types from aliases.

The source distinguishes first as a result limit from after as a continuation position. Repeating first:25 without after fits an initial-page or restart request, not advancement after the received cursor. Adding numeric filter prerequisites does not make page size carry hidden cursor state.

The source returns endCursor for the next after argument when hasNextPage is true. Retaining the now-explicitly compatible numeric filter and first:25 continues the same query criteria. Cursor continuation does not repair an invalid scalar input by itself and does not guarantee a frozen snapshot across changing data.
